### Alignment A1: the ground truth of the hand-written mappings in examples 121-139, part by part, anchored or internal

change `yomwzkpyqppx` · [log `c5ebbf1d1bd8`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/11f93b59-b830-4090-8775-33313957ef5c/c5ebbf1d1bd82395979551376b5173609ba61b007296656393ebd4868349c01b.jsonl.gz)

examples/tools/alignment/ground-truth.json breaks the mappings people wrote for the B9 examples 121-139 (--before-target, --before-arguments, --results-agree-when) into parts: one per renamed or moved method, per old input (the receiver first), per new input without a counterpart, and per result. Each input is anchored (the same parameter in both versions, whose mapping is fixed to itself: where an offset mapping must be impossible), internal (a representation that changed, which inference may relate) or new (left free); each result is equal, compared by component (a record that gained one), or changed (a person's decision). Scopes are recorded as a person's decisions, not mappings. 19 examples, 85 parts. The page examples/tools/alignment/README.md defines the scores later steps get against it: found, asked, wrong, missed, and wrong-and-accepted counted on its own.
